A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sequential data-valuation framework and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained experiments and reorganized theoretical material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original selection experiments on eight datasets and controlled message-passing experiments examining data substitutability, including Figures 3–6 and Appendix J.

after.justification: V2 retains original classical experiments and adds budget-500 evaluations, surrogate-prediction experiments, and LLM fine-tuning results and embedding ablations.

M1.justification: V2 adds the BipCov adaptation: an embedding-based top-L similarity graph, greedy reference coverage, and mean-similarity filling after coverage saturates (Appendix J.7). This substantially extends v1's fitted, label-matched distance-threshold graph procedure. Threshold fitting is also reported as minimizing MSE rather than the absolute error specified in v1 Algorithm 2; the core exact-DP selection algorithm remains equivalent.

E1.justification: V2 adds instruction-selection and LLM fine-tuning coverage through DATE-LM, using Tulu 3 instruction data and evaluating MMLU, GSM8K, and BBH. These introduce knowledge and reasoning tasks beyond the retained eight classical datasets and synthetic substitutability experiment.

E2.justification: The nine classical comparison methods remain. V2 adds evaluated Linear and MLP predictors in the surrogate comparison (Table 3), and BM25, Rep-Sim, RDS+, Grad-Sim, and LESS in the LLM comparisons (Tables 6–7). These are substantive additions to the evaluated comparator sets.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a budget-500 protocol reporting mean accuracy across selection sizes 1–500. Its new LLM protocol selects 10,000 of 200,000 instructions, performs two-epoch LoRA training of Llama-3.1-8B, and uses task-specific zero-, eight-, and three-shot evaluation. It also introduces shared-subset surrogate-error comparisons with fitted-intercept controls. The original small-budget dataset splits are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds direct analysis of surrogate prediction quality using training/test MAE and MSE (Table 3), plus seven embedding variants testing representation choice for BipCov (Table 8). Conversely, v1's six-level curvature plots are condensed to endpoint panels in v2 Figure 3, omitting the intermediate plotted evidence.

E5.justification: Classical per-dataset reporting remains mean and standard deviation over 20 runs. V2 specifies three fine-tuning seeds for its headline LLM comparison and distinguishes these results from single-seed baseline and embedding experiments. The aggregate Std Dev row from v1 Table 1 is omitted in v2 Table 9; no new significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: V2 adds budget-500 results, surrogate errors, and LLM results, including BipCov's 63.89±0.34% average versus RDS+'s 62.88±0.25% in Table 6. In the matched small-budget tables, DVRL values change, including bbc-embeddings from 0.560 to 0.653, and aggregate averages are corrected, including Bipartite from 0.041 to 0.750. Most other per-dataset entries remain unchanged; the new settings do not establish improvements over v1 under identical conditions.

T1.justification: V1's common efficiency-constrained regression argument is replaced by separate Shapley, Banzhaf, and Beta Shapley formulations and proofs, including centered features and parameter restrictions (v2 Appendices B–D). V1 Appendix G's exact greedy-optimality theorem is replaced by a conditional (1-epsilon)(1-1/e) approximation theorem in v2 Appendix H. Normalization assumptions and the distinction between optimal subsets and optimal sequence prefixes are also corrected or formalized.

C1.justification: V1's abstract and Section 5 claim greedy optimality when the surrogate accurately learns the utility. V2 narrows this to approximation guarantees under sufficient conditions. It also expands the headline empirical contribution to large-scale LLM fine-tuning, while retaining the central sequential-selection and ADP interpretation.

C2.justification: V2 replaces claims of directly controlling curvature and validating quadratic decay with a qualitative substitutability-proxy interpretation. It explains that low MSE does not establish the uniform conditions required by its guarantee. New LLM qualifications disclose potential reference-label leakage and coverage saturation after only 1–5 selections, making most remaining selections depend on the similarity fallback.

D1.justification: V2 adds a public-code pointer, classical CPU and DVRL configuration disclosures, and graph-search implementation details. Appendix J.7 supplies extensive LLM data preparation, reference construction, embedding, LoRA, evaluation, hardware, and timing information, including distinguishing timed H100 runs from H200 headline runs. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around semi-values, submodular optimization, optimization from samples, datamodel/DsDm surrogates, and efficient valuation methods. Appendix A adds many substantive citations and explicitly distinguishes the approach from GraphFilter. The earlier detailed ADP literature survey is also replaced.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, theory exposition, and experimental narrative are substantially rewritten. Preliminaries are reorganized around explicit assumptions, regression characterization is separated from policy equivalence, and detailed RQ1 discussion moves to Appendix M. The appendix structure is extensively reorganized, including moving the DP algorithm from Appendix B to Appendix L.

P2.justification: V1's full DP comparison curves are replaced by a compact summary table, and its six-setting curvature figures become a smaller endpoint display. V2 redraws the main selection curves with revised styling and adds tables for larger budgets, surrogate errors, regression formulations, computational costs, LLM comparisons, and embedding ablations. The retained detailed results table also changes its summary-row structure.

improvement.justification: Replacing v1's exact greedy-optimality claim and common efficiency-constrained regression argument with appropriately qualified formulations and proofs substantially improves the central theoretical support. Corrected result summaries, utility diagnostics, and fuller experimental documentation further strengthen the paper. Some detailed original curves disappear, and the LLM evidence has disclosed leakage and coverage-saturation limitations, but these tradeoffs do not outweigh the substantial corrections.
